before: The appointment came with a seal, a coat, and a list. The list is the company: ten names from three regions, owed to Ironwake under the armistice. None of them has arrived. I read it every morning anyway. So far it is the only part of the job I have done.

The keep is two days east. Someone has followed me since the ford, and the waystation ahead has a fort with its gate still on. A fort keeps the weather off. It does not keep anyone from shooting at it.
What the crown taught me before it sent me, which was not a lot: read the blow before you swing it. Know who answers back and who cannot. A sword answers a sword. It does not answer a bow.
(forecast <unit> <target> prints a strike and its counter before you take it. threat <unit> prints who can reach you next phase. recall rewinds to a player turn you name; you have three.)
after: Three dead on a road nobody will remember. I have nobody to add to the list yet, which is its own kind of report.
The waystation keeper says a Kestrow chaplain bound for Ironwake was taken off the mill road two days back. Her name is on my list. East it is, by way of the mill.

before: The mill road follows a stream that outlived its mill. The men who took the chaplain lost her two nights ago, the keeper says, and she has been holding the miller's house on the far bank since. Alone, two days. That is longer than I have managed anything.
Her name is on my list: Maud, Kestrow, chaplain. The list does not say whether she can fight. It says she mends things.
(This map is lost if Maud falls. She strikes at range 1 or 2 with Radiance and heals with her Salve. A fight within 6 tiles of a sleeping group wakes it; threat names what a stop would wake.)
after: Maud asked whether I was hurt before she asked my name. Then she said a prayer over the men we had killed, which I had not expected and did not stop.
Two names on the list are standing in the same place now. I read it twice this morning to be sure.

pitch.keziah: Everyone here is offering you a promise. Mine's hungry, and you'll hear it ask.
pitch.rook: She's the last one. Pick me and you're the second person alive who knows her name.

before: Hollin is a sworn village, a day short of the keep. Nobody in it is hungry. Nobody is fighting. Every hearth is lit, which is more than Ironwake can say. Nobody will meet my eye.
I asked a girl at the well her name. She said, "We're well, thank you," and went back to the bucket.
Past Hollin the keep is in sight across a field and a river. The rime on its walls has started to run.
(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Defeat the Sworn Captain. Each group sleeps until a fight comes within its hearing.)

The keeper at Sorrel Bend has stopped writing. Maud's order kept the lazar house there until the armistice, then called its sisters home and left the sick with him. Maud packs the basin. "The carts come at dusk. Keep the strippers off the door till then. You won't be thanked."

(Hold out six turns. The lanes in are announced. A unit that ends its move on the bar beside a lane, 8,1 north or 10,4 east, closes that lane for the rest of the map. The ford south cannot be barred.)
after: The carts come at dusk. They find the keeper in the well-house, and the meal bins full, bought by someone who never signed the book. Forty beds, twelve in use. "I'm angry at my order. It won't break tonight. Who here hasn't eaten?" She says the prayer over every bed, then over the keeper, with his name in it.

before: (Bet Lowry asks for one day and three of the company. Take the gatehouse: Bet on its seat at 8,3 wins. The map is lost if she falls.)
quests.ending: Bet Lowry swore first, the one the oath could not hold, choosing it.

before: Maud is going to the first shrine, a half-day off the weir road and older than the split. No rite-keeper alive has been inside. The causeway in is trodden to mud this month. "Somebody's put a man in the door. Move him. I'm going up to the altar."
(Get Maud onto the altar at 7,0 by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if she falls. Pursuers cross the causeway at 7,6 from turn 2, announced; a unit that waits where it began its phase braces.)
after: Maud kneels at the altar and says the rite, the words in order. At the response she stops. She stays on her knees longer than any prayer takes, listening, then says the response again with one word changed. On the road back she goes down the line looking at hands, and treats the frostbite first.
(Maud carries Maud's Psalter now: a heal at range 1 to 2, bound to her. Its art, Unasked, doubles a heal on an ally who has not moved or acted, and that ally's phase ends where it stands.)

before: The shrine-school at Aldmere burned around Pell when she was fourteen. The roof never went back on, and the rain has had eight years at the shelves. Now somebody brings torches for what it left. "Whatever's dry comes out. The catalogue's chained under the lectern, so I'll know what we leave."

(Get Pell off the east edge, 12,3 to 12,5, by the end of turn 7; anyone still on the board when she exits is left behind and falls. The map is lost if she falls. Three chests hold what the fire missed. The burners come in from the west road from turn 1, announced.)
after: Pell comes out with the catalogue under her arm, the chain still hanging off it. On the road she reads it through and marks the margin beside every book that stayed behind. That night she starts on the first of them from memory.

before: Somebody came down the undercroft stair after the raid with a lamp and a can of oil. The door opens only to the garrison; Pell enlisted for that door, and has the key off the quartermaster before the captain finishes saying yes. "Keep them on the stair. I want the desk read before anyone brings the oil back down."

(Get Pell onto the reading desk at 16,4 by the end of turn 7. The map is lost if she falls. The sworn come down the stair at 1,10 from turn 2, announced. Two groups sleep in the stacks and the cells; walls do not stop them hearing.)
after: Above the reading desk the charter is cut in the shrine script. Pell counts the anchor rings before she reads it: more rings than chains. Then, aloud: "Let the iron keep it from waking, and let us keep the iron." Nothing more on the stair. At the top she reads it again to the whole company, before anyone sits.
(Pell carries Pell's Commonplace now: Cinder's numbers, bound to her, and it never catches. Its art, Read Ahead, reaches one tile further for 2 less Power.)

before: Teodor asked for a day and one pair of hands. His grandfather stood watch on a hill above Aldmere for thirty years, and is buried under it. Sworn men have been digging there since the spring.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Defeat their captain on the cairn's fort at 7,0 by the end of turn 9. The map is lost if Teodor falls. The cairn's door at 7,2 is one tile wide. More come up the hill behind you from turn 3, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: what the sworn were digging for, and what the lance does in his hands at the cairn.)
(The Family Lance's last stage waited on this. It wakes once Teodor has fought enough with it, now or later.)

before: Ottilie asked for a day and one pair of hands. Her house's bills were marked paid at a counting house on the Sallow canal, and nobody there will say who signed for the money.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Rout: every enemy falls by the end of turn 11. The map is lost if Ottilie falls. The canal is crossed only at the bridges, 6,1 and 6,7; a bow reaches over it and a sword does not. More come up the near bank from turn 2, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: the ledger in the strongroom, and the seal at the foot of the page.)

before: Ottilie asked for a night and one pair of hands. The seal on the counting house's page was Hask's, and his own books sit in a Sallow bookroom two days east. Nobody in the regions will believe a copy.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Escape: Ottilie leaves by the east road, 14,3 to 14,5, by the end of turn 8; whoever is still on the board then is lost, so the ally leaves first. The map is lost if Ottilie falls. Dusk: sight is 4 on turn 1 and one less each turn, never under 1; nobody strikes what their side cannot see. Riders come down the road behind you from turn 2, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: the books on a table in a Sallow square, and the people reading their own villages' names in Hask's hand.)
(Ottilie carries Ottilie's Tally now: the Iron Bow's numbers, bound to her. Its art, Paid in Full, looses one arrow at +6 Power and -25 Acc that never doubles.)

before: Rook asks for a day and one pair of hands. The chapter keeps its roll of seats in a house on the crag above the gorge. Her name went onto it under the extra seat, the year somebody paid for that seat. "I want to read who. They watch the bridge up there. Nobody watches the sky."

(Seize: Rook stands on the roll room, 12,1, by the end of turn 8; its one door is 12,2. The map is lost if Rook falls. A flier crosses the gorge; on foot, only the road bridge crosses the gorge. A bow crit grounds a flier; over water she then cannot move. Pursuers from turn 2, announced.)
after: The last page of the roll is the chapter's claim to the extra seat. Pinned under it, a receipt: paid in full, in new keep silver. Under that, the drake's number, and Rook's name on the line below. "Your keep bought a seat with us." She folds the receipt into her glove and leaves the roll open.
(The Drover is open to Rook at her second promotion: the other door above the Skyrider.)

before: Teodor asked for two days and one pair of hands. The prison's outer gate is a day north of Aldmere, under the hill, and the first warden's name is cut over it. Hask's sworn have been chipping at the stone around it for shards.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Defeat their captain on the fort before the gate, 7,2, by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Teodor falls. The old wall at row 5 has two ways through: a one-tile gap at 4,5 and a breach at 10,5 and 11,5. Riders keep the east yard. More come up the road behind you from turn 3, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: the name over the gate, and the lance that matches it.)

(The Family Lance is the First Warden's Lance now. Once woken, its art Turn the Key strikes at -4 Power, once, never doubling; a hit the enemy survives locks it, Mov 0 until its side's next phase ends, while Teodor stands beside it. If he leaves or falls, the lock drops to a chill.)

before: Keziah asked for a day and one pair of hands. Her mother's shrine stands on a knoll off the west road, burned three times, once by each region. Someone is stripping the lead off what is left of its roof.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Rout: defeat every enemy by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Keziah falls. The ring wall has a west door at 4,3 and a breach at 7,5. More come up the road from turn 3, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: the hearth, the ash, and what Keziah leaves on it.)

before: Rook asks for one more day. The ledger in the rookery's loft, on the fells above the chapter house, still lists one cold drake as a holding and one rider on the line below. The roost is full of the church's wingriders. "I know every one of them by how they land. They'll follow. Let them."

(Escape: get everyone off the east edge, 14,4 to 14,6, by the end of turn 9. Rook leaving wins the map, and anyone still on the board is left behind as fallen, so Rook leaves last. The map is lost if Rook falls. On foot only the bridge at 7,5 and 8,5 crosses the ravine; an enemy bow's crit grounds Rook; over water she then cannot move. Riders from the rookery behind from turn 2, announced.)
after: Rook strikes the holding line in the loft's ledger, then her own, and leaves the pen across the page. Halfway down the fell, to the drake: "It was only us two on that page, and now there's no page, and I'm lonely, with you breathing down my neck." The drake leans on her the rest of the way.

before: Keziah knows the man on the door. Joab kept the lamps at her mother's shrine; he is sworn now. Hask has sent an envoy to the old outland stone on the moor, offering her people a seat and a god, and Joab stands bound to the envoy.

(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Defeat Boss: defeat the envoy, who keeps the fort at 12,3, by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Keziah falls. Joab holds the yard's west door at 9,4, bound to the envoy: if the envoy falls first, Joab lays down the axe, freed. A breach in the south wall at 11,7 is the long way round. More come up behind you from turn 5, announced.)
after: (Placeholder until the writing pass: the stone, the oath said over it, and which side of the hunger it was said on.)

hires.name: Corin Ashby
hires.line: Took the bounty because the harvest failed. Says so.

hires.name: Bet Lowry
hires.line: Twenty years on a town gate. Has opinions about gates.

hires.name: Ines Tarrow
hires.line: Hunts for a living. Charges extra for people.

hires.name: Mattias Grue
hires.line: Failed out of a shrine school. Kept the books.

hires.name: Tamsin Hale
hires.line: Left her parish over a roof. Won the argument, lost the roof.

hires.name: Wat Dunmore
hires.line: Sold his horse twice. Bought it back once.

hires.name: Edda Vane
hires.line: Flew dispatches for a war that ended. Nobody wrote to tell her.
